html:
The Ljubljana earthquake struck on 14 April 1895, Easter Sunday, and damaged most of the buildings in the city, then a provincial capital of Austria Hungary.

About ten people died, but many buildings were so damaged they had to be torn down. The mayor Ivan Hribar used the rebuilding to turn Ljubljana into a modern Slovene capital, with new streets, schools and Art Nouveau facades, many designed by architects trained in Vienna. Electric light and a tram followed. The new city gave Slovenes a capital that looked like their own, setting the scene for the work of Jože Plečnik after 1918.
